$schema_note: Open-data reference for the Johnson solids in this registry whose construction needed something beyond a single closed-form apex-height equation -- a discrete registration search, a combinatorial face-selection rule, or a multi-step operation composed from smaller verified pieces. Companion to docs/johnson-solids-constructions.md (human-readable) and docs/build-plan.md (full narrative postmortems). Every numeric claim here was verified computationally in this project (scipy ConvexHull + this registry's own validateShape/verify:face-attach/verify:face-twist scripts) before being recorded -- see 'verification' per entry.
license_note: Same license as the parent repository (see LICENSE).

target_face_selector.rule: the unique triangular face of J63 that is edge-adjacent to all 3 of its pentagonal faces
target_face_selector.method: combinatorial: for each of J63's 5 triangles, count shared edges with each of its 3 pentagons; exactly one triangle scores 3

registration.note: trivial -- a triangle's 3-fold symmetry makes all 3 discrete registrations equivalent by symmetry, verified not assumed

prior_wrong_attempt.what: augmenting a PENTAGON face with a pentagonal pyramid
prior_wrong_attempt.why_wrong: provably forced back onto J62 (a regular pentagon's matching pyramid apex position has no freedom)

J66.name: augmented_truncated_cube

target_face_selector.rule: any one of the truncated cube's 6 octagonal faces (all equivalent by symmetry)

registration.note: an octagon has 8 discrete registrations; exactly the ODD offsets (relative to computeFaceAttach's own theta0 baseline) produce the correct result -- the cupola's own squares must land adjacent to the truncated cube's TRIANGLES, not its own larger faces
registration.wrong_offset_symptom: one pre-existing truncated-cube triangle becomes exactly coplanar with an adjacent cupola triangle and merges into a RHOMBUS (unit edges, unequal diagonals sqrt(3) vs 1), not a true square

prior_wrong_attempt.what: used computeFaceAttach's default registration (offset 0, 'no extra twist from the measured base vertex')
prior_wrong_attempt.why_wrong: happened to be one of the 4 wrong offsets

verification: quad_diagonal_check (equal diagonals sqrt(2) required for a true square)

target_face_selector.rule: two of the truncated cube's 6 octagonal faces, specifically the OPPOSITE pair (dot(normal_a, normal_b) = -1)
target_face_selector.note: not adjacent -- confirmed by external source before building, not assumed

registration.note: each of the 2 capped faces needed its own registration verified INDEPENDENTLY (10 total registrations checked across the 2 faces) before combining -- they happened to need the same parity here, but that was checked, not assumed

target_face_selector.rule: any one of the truncated dodecahedron's 12 decagonal faces (all equivalent by symmetry)

registration.note: a decagon has 10 discrete registrations; exactly the ODD offsets produce the correct result -- identical pattern to J66, generalized from octagon to decagon

J69.name: parabiaugmented_truncated_dodecahedron

target_face_selector.rule: two decagons in the 'para' (opposite, dot=-1) class
target_face_selector.classification_scheme: the truncated dodecahedron's 12 decagons carry the SAME adjacent/meta/para face-angle classes as the plain dodecahedron (cos 0.4472 / -0.4472 / -1) -- confirmed, not assumed, since the 12 decagons correspond 1:1 to the dodecahedron's 12 faces

registration.note: verified independently per face before combining, same discipline as J67

verification: congruence_check_not_equal_to: J70_METABIAUGMENTED_TRUNCATED_DODECAHEDRON (pairwise-distance histogram, max diff 0.244, despite identical V/E/F)

target_face_selector.rule: two decagons in the 'meta' (dot approx -0.4472) class -- NOT the para pair J69 uses
three MUTUALLY-meta decagons (all 3 pairwise dot products approx -0.4472)
target_face_selector.note: 20 such triples exist by symmetry; any one works -- arbitrarily picked one

registration.note: IMPORTANT: the 3 faces did NOT all need the same registration parity -- 1 odd, 2 even. This is the concrete instance of a hazard this project had only hypothesized before (J67's own doc comment): two faces of the same solid can need different-parity registrations depending on that specific face's own vertex-0 phase. Caught only because each face was verified fully independently, not assumed to share J67's 'they happened to match' result.

J79.name: bigyrate_diminished_rhombicosidodecahedron
J79.operation: region-gyrate (x2) + region-diminish (x1), composed on the same base

region_decomposition.rule: RHOMBICOSIDODECAHEDRON decomposes into 12 local pentagonal-cupola-shaped regions, one per pentagon face, each pentagon's 5 vertices (the 'cap') surrounded by a ring of 5 triangles alternating with 5 squares (the 'waist', 10 vertices) -- extracted combinatorially from the registry's own face/edge data, not assumed
region_decomposition.classification_scheme: the 12 regions carry the SAME adjacent/meta/para face-angle classes as the dodecahedron (cos 0.4472 / -0.4472 / -1), confirmed since RD's 12 pentagons correspond 1:1 to dodecahedron faces

gyrate_operation.definition: rotate a region's 5 pentagon-cap vertices by exactly 36 degrees (one waist-ring step) around the axis through the solid's center and the pentagon's own centroid, keeping the 10 waist vertices fixed
gyrate_operation.regions_gyrated: the 'meta' pair (dot approx -0.4472) -- NOT the 'para' (opposite) pair
gyrate_operation.self_check: reproduces J72_GYRATE_RHOMBICOSIDODECAHEDRON exactly for a single region (0.000000 unordered point-set error) and J73_PARABIGYRATE_RHOMBICOSIDODECAHEDRON exactly for a para pair (5e-13 error, floating-point noise) -- validated against already-registered shapes BEFORE trusting the operation for J79's own (different) region pair

diminish_operation.definition: remove a region's 5 pentagon-cap vertices entirely, exposing its 10-vertex waist ring as a real decagon face once the convex hull recomputes
diminish_operation.region_selection_constraint: the diminished region's waist ring must share ZERO vertices with either gyrated region's pentagon cap -- of the 10 regions remaining after picking the meta pair, exactly 2 satisfy this (both classified 'meta' to both gyrated regions, i.e. non-adjacent, matching the external description 'none of the cupolae being adjacent')
diminish_operation.self_check: reproduces J76_DIMINISHED_RHOMBICOSIDODECAHEDRON exactly for a single region, confirmed via rotation-invariant pairwise-distance histogram (max diff 8.9e-16) since J76's own stored orientation differs from RD's (an arbitrary choice from whichever batch built it, not a geometric discrepancy)

prior_wrong_attempt.what: gyrated the 'para' (opposite) pair, reasoning it should reproduce J73's own already-verified construction, then tried diminishing each of the 10 remaining regions
prior_wrong_attempt.why_wrong: the external source's 'non-opposite' wording was misread as satisfied by the para pair; it actually excludes it. Checked combinatorially: the para pair's pentagon caps overlap ALL 10 remaining regions' waist rings (a structural fact of RD's vertex configuration -- every vertex belongs to exactly one pentagon), which is exactly why all 10 diminish attempts failed identically (max edge length 3.05 in every case) -- not a coincidence needing transform-tracing, a real geometric impossibility from the wrong premise
prior_wrong_attempt.note: this wrong reading was made TWICE independently -- once in the original batch 9 attempt, once again in this project's own batch-10 scoping doc before the source was re-read precisely -- worth remembering that citing an external source doesn't by itself guarantee correct interpretation of it
